title: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager: assess Microsoft Foundry agents against AI regulations
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, Foundry integration behaviour and licensing statements are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge Microsoft's conflicting assessment-role guidance, complete the control paths and remove the checklist instruction whose permissions control is not in the table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Compliance Manager integration for assessing agents created in Microsoft Foundry.
claims.quote: This feature in Purview Compliance Manager shall enable customers to automatically access the compliance posture of Agents created in AI Foundry.

claims.claim: The planned integration maps Foundry agents to compliance regulations and assessments.
claims.quote: Customers can map Agents being created in AI Foundry to compliance regulations and assessments in Purview Compliance Manager

claims.claim: The roadmap describes reporting compliance status and improvement actions for Foundry agents.
claims.quote: get to know the compliance status and improvement actions to be innovative and compliant.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn describes the Foundry integration without marking it In development, Preview or generally available.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager Foundry automated actions convert manual Testing source default integration; opened compliance-manager-assessments. Its Automatic Assessments section describes integration and prerequisites without a release-status label.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Foundry integration's tenant-level arrival default is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager Foundry integration default enabled six months Copilot Agent licenses pricing meter manual actions Testing source; opened assessments and setup. Setup states eligible-action testing defaults, not whether the Foundry integration arrives enabled.

claims.claim: No source states that arrival of this integration changes existing tenant behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager Foundry automated actions convert manual Testing source default integration; opened assessments and setup and read roadmap description. No passage states an automatic change to existing assessments when this integration arrives.

claims.claim: The remaining Foundry actions are not described as automated.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager Foundry automated actions convert manual Testing source default integration; opened assessments and read its full Foundry section. It identifies 15 of 75 actions as automated and describes no automation for the remainder.

claims.claim: Access to evaluation data in Compliance Manager follows its role-based permissions.
claims.quote: Compliance Manager uses a role-based access control (RBAC) permission model. Only users who are assigned a role can access Compliance Manager, and the actions allowed by each user are restricted by role type.

claims.claim: Users need at least Compliance Manager Reader or Microsoft Entra Global reader access.
claims.quote: Users need at least the Compliance Manager reader role, or Microsoft Entra global reader role, to access Compliance Manager.

claims.claim: Access can be granted for individual assessments through Manage user access.
claims.quote: From your Assessments page, find the assessment you want to grant access to. Select it to open its details page. In the upper-right corner, select Manage user access.

claims.claim: Learn lists Compliance Manager Administration, Compliance Manager Assessor or Global Administrator for creating and modifying assessments.
claims.quote: To create and modify an assessment, a user must hold a role of Compliance Manager Administration, Compliance Manager Assessor, or Global Administrator.
claims.fix: Add after this role list: 'Microsoft's setup page disagrees: it says Compliance Manager Assessor can edit data but cannot create assessments, while Compliance Manager Contribution can create them.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/compliance-manager-setup#role-types.

claims.claim: Adding Foundry agents during assessment creation requires Azure AI Project Manager or Azure AI User on the relevant Foundry accounts.
claims.quote: The admin account must have either the Azure AI Project Manager or Azure AI User RBAC role assigned to the relevant AI Foundry accounts.

claims.claim: Foundry agents are added during assessment creation.
claims.quote: The Azure AI Project Manager or Azure AI User RBAC role access is required to add Agents during assessment creation for the AI Foundry service in Compliance Manager.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Azure AI User and Azure AI Project Manager were renamed Foundry User and Foundry Project Manager respectively.
claims.quote: Foundry User, Foundry Owner, Foundry Account Owner, and Foundry Project Manager were previously named Azure AI User, Azure AI Owner, Azure AI Account Owner, and Azure AI Project Manager.

claims.claim: The GUID 53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d identifies Foundry User.
claims.quote: Foundry User: 53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Compliance Manager > Assessments > Add assessment reaches the assessment creation wizard.
claims.quote: From your Assessments page, select Add assessment to begin the assessment creation wizard.
claims.fix: The path starts creation but stops before completing it. Extend it to 'Compliance Manager > Assessments > Add assessment > Base your assessment on a regulation > Select regulation > regulation > Add name and group > Select services > Select services > service > Review and finish > Create assessment', using the wizard labels at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/compliance-manager-assessments#create-assessments. Keep the note that Foundry agents are added during creation; do not invent a Foundry-specific agent-picker label.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for creating Compliance Manager assessments.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Compliance Manager create assessment API PowerShell Security Compliance Microsoft Graph. Read assessments and Graph threat-assessment excerpts: portal creation or unrelated threat assessment APIs, not a Compliance Manager create API.

claims.claim: Azure portal > Foundry resource > Access control (IAM) reaches Foundry role assignment management.
claims.quote: In the Azure portal, open your Foundry resource and go to Access control (IAM). Create a role assignment for Foundry User, set Members to User, group, or service principal, select your user principal
claims.fix: Complete the path as 'Foundry resource > Access control (IAM) > Role assignments > Add > Add role assignment > Role > Job function roles > Foundry User > Members > User, group, or service principal > Select members > user'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments-portal for the intermediate IAM steps; the Foundry role is documented at the existing docs URL.

claims.claim: az role assignment create --role 53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d --assignee <user> --scope <foundry-resource-id> assigns Foundry User at the relevant Foundry resource scope.
claims.quote: Assign the Foundry User role on your Foundry resource to your user principal. [...] az role assignment create --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --assignee "joe@contoso.com" --scope

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Compliance Manager > Testing source reaches automated testing settings.
claims.quote: select the Settings icon at the top of the page, then select Compliance Manager. [...] Select Testing source from the left navigation. [...] Turn off automatic testing for all actions.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Settings > Compliance Manager > Testing source > Turn off automatic testing for all actions'. The same page also documents the alternative options 'Turn on automatic testing for all actions' and 'Turn on automatic testing per action'; name these in the note if retaining the row's general on/off wording.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for changing the Compliance Manager Testing source setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Compliance Manager Testing source automatic testing PowerShell API; opened setup and read improvement-actions and Check-PurviewConfig excerpts. The results document portal testing settings and unrelated diagnostics, not a setter API.

claims.claim: Testing source controls automatic testing for eligible improvement actions generally.

claims.claim: Compliance Manager Administrator or Global Administrator can access settings and change automated testing.
claims.quote: The Compliance Manager Administrator and the Global Administrator for your organization can change the settings for automated testing at any time.

claims.claim: The Foundry documentation does not explicitly identify Testing source as its specific automatic-to-manual conversion route.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager Foundry automated actions convert manual Testing source default integration. Read assessments, setup and improvement-actions excerpts: Foundry names settings; other pages describe general settings and Testing type, not the Foundry-specific mapping.
